title: Cap. VI Arg. 8: Arminians twist the gift — sufficient grace to persevere if they will
pass_a_gloss: This argument greatly tortures both Arminians and Jesuits. The Arminians therefore would not dare openly to deny that persevering faith is the gift of God, yet they strenuously deny that that action by which God gives us faith is always efficacious, certain, and invincible. And further they teach that when God gives men the power of arriving at him, faith is already prepared for them as a gift, provided this grace be continued. Without doubt they think the same of perseverance, namely that by this gift nothing else is designated than that sufficient grace by which power is given to men of persevering if they will. But such a gift does not argue a preceding destination to eternal life; because in this way faith and perseverance is given to those who never had, nor will have, either faith, or perseverance, or eternal life.
pass_b_english: This argument badly torments Arminians and Jesuits alike. Arminians dare not openly deny that persevering faith is God's gift — yet they strongly deny that the act by which God gives faith is always efficacious, certain, and invincible. They teach that when God gives men power to reach him, faith is already prepared as a gift if that grace continues. Doubtless they hold the same of perseverance: the 'gift' means only sufficient grace — power to persevere if they will. That kind of gift does not imply prior destination to eternal life; it is 'given' even to those who never had and never will have faith, perseverance, or eternal life.
source_text: Hoc argumentum valde torquet tam Arminianos quam Jesuitas. Arminiani itaque non ausint aperte negare, fidem perseverantem esse donum Dei, tamen strenue negant, actionem eam per quam Deus nobis fidem donat, semper efficacem, certam, et invictam esse. Atque porro docent, quando Deus dat hominibus potentiam ad ipsum perveniendi, fidem jam esse iisdem paratam ut donum, modo continuetur haec gratia. Proculdubio idem sentiunt de perseverantia, nempe hoc dono nil aliud designari quam illam sufficientem gratiam, qua datur hominibus potentia perseverandi si velint. Tale autem donum non arguit praeeuntem destinationem ad vitam aeternam; quia hoc modo fides et perseverantia donatur illis, qui nec fidem, nec perseverantiam, nec vitam aeternam unquam habuerunt aut habituri sunt.
